_comment: Tolerances for piece p-mars-atmo, compared against p-mars-atmo.real.csv (Viking 1 Lander entry profile, Seiff & Kirk 1977, NASA PDS Atmospheres Node). Altitude is km above the Viking-era Mars reference surface (the ~6.1 mbar areoid), not the MOLA areoid; the VL1 landing site sits at -1.49 km on this scale (about -3.6 km MOLA). Density and pressure use relative tolerances because they span 7 orders of magnitude; the equivalent log10 bound is also given. The bands are wide because one entry profile is one time and place: Viking 2 (landed 1976-09-03, 48N) differs from Viking 1 (1976-07-20, 22N) by 0.68-1.01x in density over 30-110 km, and later entries (Pathfinder 1997, MSL 2012) differ by up to about 2x above 60 km (tides, season, dust).

bands.why: Surface pressure varies about +/-12% seasonally (CO2 cycle, Viking lander barometers). The shift between the Viking datum and the MOLA datum (~2 km) changes density by ~18% at H~11 km. Below 25 km the VL1 data are sparse parachute-phase points.
VL2/VL1 density ratio here is 0.73-1.01. Later entries fall inside a ~1.5x envelope.

VL2/VL1 ratio is 0.68-0.88. Thermal tides and seasonal inflation of the upper atmosphere give roughly 2x variation between entries. Accelerometer noise is large above ~110 km. 121-129 km is log-interpolated between the accelerometer's top (120.19 km) and UAMS at 130 km.

density_kgm3.note: Pass if |sim/real - 1| <= tol_rel for the band (or |log10(sim/real)| <= tol_log10). Compare on log scale.

pressure_Pa.note: Source gives pressure in mbar; the CSV converts it to Pa (x100). Pressure comes from hydrostatic integration of the measured density, so it carries the same spread as density.

bands.why: VL1 vs VL2 differ by <=10 K at 30-40 km. The diurnal range near the surface is much larger (~50-60 K at the ground), but the entry profile is late afternoon.
VL1 shows ~+/-15 K wave structure (tides/gravity waves) that a smooth model will not reproduce. VL2 differs by up to 43 K at 105-110 km, and Pathfinder was ~20-30 K colder near 80 km.

temperature_K.note: A smooth model is expected to track the mean trend (~230 K near 0 km falling to ~140-150 K at 60-120 km), not the wave structure.

surface_density_kgm3_at_0km.note: VL1 value at z=0 (parachute-phase point at 0.133 km: 0.01498; at the landing site z=-1.49 km: 0.0168). The commonly quoted global-mean surface density is ~0.020 kg/m3 (NASA Mars Fact Sheet), which is inside the tolerance only at its edge, because it refers to the mean datum/season.

surface_pressure_Pa_at_0km.note: VL1 6.707 mbar at z=0.01 km (7.62 mbar at the landing site). The NASA Mars Fact Sheet global mean is 636 Pa (6.36 mbar), 5% lower; both pass.

scale_height_km_0_20km.note: Viking 1 near-surface pressure scale height H0 = 11.697 km (Seiff & Kirk 1977 Table II note; VL2 11.363 km). The density e-folding over 0-20 km in the CSV is ~12.0 km. The NASA fact sheet gives 11.1 km.
